A.text: Identify the logic operation carried out by the following circuit
A.sol_text:
Answer: (4)
Solution:

Y = A̅B̅ = A̅ + B̅
Y = A + B

The circuit shows:
- Input A passes through a NOT gate (NAND gate with one inverted output shown as A̅)
- Input B passes through a NOT gate (NAND gate with one inverted output shown as B̅)
- The outputs A̅ and B̅ are fed into an OR gate
- Final output Y = A̅ + B̅

By De Morgan's Law: A̅ + B̅ = A̅B̅ (which is NOR)
However, applying De Morgan's again: A + B = A + B (which is OR)

Therefore, the logic operation is OR, making the answer (4).

A.text: A series circuit consisting of a capacitor and a coil with active resistance is connected to a source of harmonic voltage whose frequency can be varied, keeping the voltage amplitude constant. Similarly, I_M₂ = V_M / √(R² + (ω₂L - 1/(ω₂C))²)

Since, both I_M₁ are n times less than resonance current amplitude,
∴ I_M₁ = I_M₂

∴ V_M / √(R² + (ωL - 1/(ω₁C))²) = V_M / √(R² + (ω₂L - 1/(ω₂C))²) or ω₁L - 1/(ω₁C) = 1/(ω₂C) - ω₂L

or (ω₁²LC - 1)/(ω₁C) = (1 - ω₂²LC)/(ω₂C)

or ω₁ω₂LC(ω₁ + ω₂) - (ω₁ + ω₂) = 0

or 1 - ω₁ω₂LC = 0

∴ ω₁ω₂ = 1/(LC) = ω₀²

B.subject: Physics
B.text: For a series LCR circuit, at resonance frequency (ω₀), inductive reactance is ω₀L = (2/√3)R, where R is the resistance in the circuit and P₀ is the power dissipated across the circuit. If now operating frequency increased to ω = 2ω₀ and P is the power dissipation across the circuit, then find the ratio P₀/P.
B.sol_text:
At resonance |z| = R ω₀L = (2/√3)R

and P₀ = v₀²/R and ω₀L = 1/(ω₀C)

At frequency ω = 2ω₀, z = R + (2ω₀L - 1/(2ω₀C))ĵ

⇒ z = R + ω₀L(3/2)ĵ

∴ |z|² = R² + (9/4)(3/4)·R²

⇒ |z|² = 4R²

⇒ |z| = 2R

∴ I = v₀/|z|

Now P = V.I.cosθ

P = V₀·(v₀)/(2R)·(1/2) = v₀²/(4R)

So, P₀/P = 4
B.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

A.text:
The reaction of (CH₃)₂C─CH₂ with CH₃OH in (i) acid H⁺, and (ii) base CH₃O⁻, respectively give

(1) (CH₃)₂C(OCH₃)CH₂OH and (CH₃)₂C(OH)CH₂OCH₃

(2) (CH₃)₂C(OCH₃)CH₂OH and (CH₃)₂C(OCH₃)CH₂OH

(3) (CH₃)₂C(OCH₃)CH₂OCH₃ and (CH₃)₂C(CH₃)₂C(OH)CH₂OH

(4) (CH₃)₂C(OH)CH₂OH and (CH₃)₂C(OCH₃)CH₂OCH₃
A.sol_text:
Answer: (1)

Solution:

[Mechanism showing acid-catalyzed reaction]
Epoxide + H⁺ → Protonated epoxide with oxonium
Protonated epoxide + CH₃OH → (CH₃)₂C(OCH₃)CH₂OH

[Mechanism showing base-catalyzed reaction]
Epoxide + CH₃O⁻/CH₃OH → (CH₃)₂C(OH)CH₂OCH₃

In acid conditions: The more substituted carbon of the epoxide is attacked, leading to formation of (CH₃)₂C(OCH₃)CH₂OH

In base conditions: The less hindered (primary) carbon is attacked, leading to formation of (CH₃)₂C(OH)CH₂OCH₃

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The above transformation will be achieved by which of the following sequence of reagents?

t – BuO⁻/Δ; HBr; alc KOH/Δ; HBr/R₂O₂
A.sol_text:
Starting material has Br and a methyl group on adjacent carbons of a cyclohexene ring.

Step 1: alc KOH/Δ → Elimination of HBr gives a diene (conjugated double bond system)

Step 2: HBr → Addition of HBr to the diene gives bromide at one position with the methyl group still present

Step 3: t–BuO⁻/Δ → Elimination of HBr using strong base gives another double bond

Step 4: HBr/R₂O₂ → Anti-Markovnikov addition of HBr (peroxide effect) adds Br to the terminal carbon of the double bond, placing Br in the desired exocyclic position, giving the final product where Br is on a CH₂ group attached to the cyclohexane ring.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: In a five-team tournament, each team plays exactly one game with every other team. Each team has a 50% chance of winning any game it plays (No game ends with tie). The probability that the tournament will produce neither an undefeated team nor a winless team is
A.sol_text:
Each team has to play four games. Five teams play a total of (5·4)/2 = 10 games and each game can have two possible outcomes
∴ There are 2^10 possible outcomes
As almost one team can be undefeated let team 'A' is undefeated i.e. team A will win all four matches.
For remaining '6' match total outcomes = 2^6
Number of ways of producing an undefeated team = 5·C_1·2^6
Similarly Number of ways of producing a winless team 5·2^6
Let A be undefeated and B be winless
There are seven games in which either team A or team B or both team play and remaining three games left have two possible outcomes.
Number of possible outcomes = 2^(10-7) = 2^3 tournaments i.e. 20·2^3 = 5·2^5 of the 2^10 outcomes have both an undefeated team and a winless team
∴ Total number of ways not having winless and undefeated team 2^10 − 2.5·2^6 + 5·2^5
= 2^5(2^5 − 5·2^2 + 5) = 2^5·17
∴ Required probability = (2^5·17)/(2^10) = 17/32

Given differential equation is
yy″ = 2(y′)²

⇒ ∫(y″/y) = ∫(2/y)y′
⇒ logy′ = 2logy + loga
⇒ logy′ = log(ay²)

and -4 = 4a + b ...(ii)

⇒ b = 0
∴ -(1/y) = (-1)x + 0 ⇒ xy = 1
∴ Curve C₁: xy = 1 ...(i)
